questions.question_text: Science is best described as:

options.label: A
options.text: A systematic way of investigating the natural world

options.label: C
options.text: A fixed body of beliefs that cannot change

options.label: D
options.text: A method used only in laboratories

questions.explanation: Science is a systematic approach to understanding the natural world through observation, evidence, reasoning, and testing.

questions.question_text: Which feature is most central to scientific knowledge?
questions.explanation: Scientific knowledge is grounded in evidence and can be revised when new evidence appears.

questions.question_text: A scientific explanation should ideally be:
questions.explanation: Scientific explanations should be testable against observations or experiments.

questions.question_text: Which statement best reflects the nature of science?

options.label: A
options.text: Scientific knowledge can be refined when new evidence emerges

options.label: C
options.text: Science depends only on individual belief

questions.explanation: Science is provisional and self-correcting because conclusions can change with better evidence.

questions.question_text: Objectivity in science primarily involves:

options.label: A
options.text: Evaluating evidence without deliberately distorting it to fit personal preferences

questions.explanation: Scientific objectivity requires fair evaluation of evidence and methods.

questions.question_text: Why is repeatability important in science?

options.label: A
options.text: It allows findings to be checked independently

options.label: B
options.text: It guarantees every hypothesis is correct

options.label: C
options.text: It eliminates the need for evidence

questions.explanation: Repeatability allows other researchers to test whether findings are reliable.

questions.question_text: A hypothesis is:
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation that can be tested using evidence.

questions.question_text: Which step commonly follows the formulation of a hypothesis?

options.label: A
options.text: Testing it through observation or experiment

questions.explanation: Hypotheses are evaluated through systematic observation or experimentation.

questions.question_text: In an experiment, the variable deliberately changed by the researcher is the:
questions.explanation: The independent variable is manipulated to observe its effect on the dependent variable.

questions.question_text: The dependent variable is:

options.label: C
options.text: Always the same as the control

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the measured response to changes in the independent variable.

questions.question_text: A control group is useful because it:
questions.explanation: Controls help isolate the effect of the variable being tested.

questions.question_text: Why should scientific methods be described clearly in a report?

options.label: A
options.text: So others can understand and reproduce the investigation

options.label: B
options.text: So the experiment cannot be questioned

questions.explanation: Clear methods allow transparency, evaluation, and replication.

questions.question_text: Ancient Egyptian scientific achievement included important developments in:
questions.explanation: Ancient Egypt contributed significantly to medicine, mathematics, astronomy, and engineering.

questions.question_text: Ancient Mesopotamian scholars made notable contributions to:
questions.explanation: Mesopotamian civilisation developed early mathematical and astronomical systems.

questions.question_text: The ancient Greeks are especially associated with:
questions.explanation: Greek thinkers developed influential approaches to logic, nature, mathematics, and explanation.

questions.question_text: Hippocrates is historically associated with:
questions.explanation: Hippocrates is traditionally associated with early systematic approaches to medicine.

questions.question_text: Archimedes is associated with important work in:
questions.explanation: Archimedes made major contributions to mathematics, mechanics, and hydrostatics.

questions.question_text: Why are ancient scientific traditions important to the history of science?

options.label: A
options.text: They provided observations, methods, and ideas that influenced later knowledge

options.label: B
options.text: They had no influence on later civilisations

options.label: C
options.text: They were identical to modern science

questions.explanation: Ancient traditions contributed ideas and practices that later societies preserved, criticised, and developed further.

topics.name: Islamic and African Contributions to Science

questions.question_text: Scholars in the medieval Islamic world contributed significantly to:
questions.explanation: Scholars working across the Islamic world contributed to mathematics, medicine, astronomy, optics, and other disciplines.

questions.question_text: Al-Khwarizmi is strongly associated with the development of:
questions.explanation: Al-Khwarizmi made foundational contributions to algebra and systematic mathematical methods.

questions.question_text: Ibn al-Haytham is well known for contributions to:
questions.explanation: Ibn al-Haytham made major contributions to optics, vision, and experimental investigation.

questions.question_text: Traditional African knowledge systems often included practical understanding of:

options.label: A
options.text: Agriculture, medicine, metallurgy, and the environment

questions.explanation: African societies developed practical knowledge in agriculture, medicine, metallurgy, architecture, and environmental management.

questions.question_text: Why was the translation of scientific works historically important?

options.label: A
options.text: It helped knowledge move between cultures and generations

options.label: B
options.text: It prevented the development of new ideas

options.label: C
options.text: It removed the need for observation

questions.explanation: Translation and preservation supported intellectual continuity and cross-cultural exchange.

questions.question_text: Which statement best reflects the historical development of science?

options.label: A
options.text: Scientific knowledge developed through contributions from many civilisations

options.label: B
options.text: Science developed entirely within one civilisation

options.label: C
options.text: Ancient societies made no technological contributions

options.label: D
options.text: Scientific ideas did not move between regions

questions.explanation: The history of science reflects cumulative contributions, exchanges, criticisms, and discoveries across many societies.

topics.name: Renaissance and the Rise of Modern Science

questions.question_text: The Renaissance encouraged scientific development partly through:

options.label: A
options.text: Renewed interest in learning, observation, and inquiry

questions.explanation: The Renaissance encouraged scholarship, inquiry, and renewed engagement with nature and earlier intellectual traditions.

questions.question_text: Nicolaus Copernicus is associated with the idea that:

options.label: A
options.text: The planets revolve around the Sun

options.label: B
options.text: The Sun revolves around every planet

questions.explanation: Copernicus proposed a heliocentric model in which Earth and other planets orbit the Sun.

questions.question_text: Galileo Galilei strengthened scientific investigation by emphasising:
questions.explanation: Galileo's work helped demonstrate the power of observation, experimentation, and mathematical analysis.

questions.question_text: Johannes Kepler is known for:
questions.explanation: Kepler formulated mathematical laws describing planetary orbits.

questions.question_text: Isaac Newton made major contributions to:
questions.explanation: Newton developed influential laws of motion and universal gravitation.

questions.question_text: Why was the Scientific Revolution historically significant?

options.label: A
options.text: It strengthened systematic observation, mathematics, and experimentation in explanations of nature

options.label: C
options.text: It removed the need for theories

questions.explanation: The Scientific Revolution transformed methods and explanatory frameworks used to investigate nature.

questions.question_text: Charles Darwin is associated with the theory of:
questions.explanation: Darwin proposed natural selection as a major mechanism of biological evolution.

questions.question_text: Albert Einstein is most closely associated with:
questions.explanation: Einstein developed the special and general theories of relativity.

questions.question_text: The germ theory of disease established that:

options.label: B
options.text: Disease is always caused by weather

questions.explanation: Germ theory linked microorganisms with infectious disease.

questions.question_text: Understanding the structure of DNA was important because it helped explain:
questions.explanation: DNA structure provided a molecular basis for understanding genetic information and inheritance.

questions.question_text: Quantum theory was developed mainly to explain:

options.label: A
options.text: Phenomena at atomic and subatomic scales

questions.explanation: Quantum theory describes physical behaviour at very small scales.

questions.question_text: A scientific revolution is best understood as:

options.label: A
options.text: A major transformation in scientific concepts or explanatory frameworks

questions.explanation: Scientific revolutions involve substantial changes in dominant scientific concepts, methods, or frameworks.

questions.question_text: Philosophy of science examines:

options.label: A
options.text: The methods, assumptions, justification, and meaning of scientific knowledge

questions.explanation: Philosophy of science examines how scientific claims are produced, tested, justified, interpreted, and limited.

questions.question_text: Empiricism gives particular importance to:
questions.explanation: Empiricism emphasises observation and experience as important sources of knowledge.

questions.question_text: Rationalism gives particular importance to:
questions.explanation: Rationalism emphasises reason and logical thought in acquiring knowledge.

questions.question_text: Karl Popper argued that scientific claims should be:
questions.explanation: Popper argued that scientific propositions should be capable, in principle, of being shown false by evidence.

questions.question_text: Thomas Kuhn used the term paradigm to refer to:

options.label: A
options.text: A broad framework of concepts and practices shared by a scientific community

questions.explanation: For Kuhn, a paradigm is a framework that guides normal scientific research within a community.

questions.question_text: Why is criticism important in science?

options.label: A
options.text: It allows claims, evidence, and methods to be scrutinised and improved

questions.explanation: Critical scrutiny helps identify weaknesses, errors, and alternative explanations.

questions.question_text: Technology is best described as:

options.label: A
options.text: The practical application of knowledge and techniques to solve problems

questions.explanation: Technology applies knowledge, skills, techniques, and tools to practical problems.

questions.question_text: Science and technology are related because:

options.label: A
options.text: Scientific knowledge can support technology, while technology can enable scientific investigation

questions.explanation: Scientific discoveries can lead to technologies, while new technologies often enable new scientific discoveries.

questions.question_text: Vaccination is an example of science affecting society through:
questions.explanation: Vaccination applies biomedical knowledge to the prevention and control of disease.

questions.question_text: One social challenge associated with technology is:
questions.explanation: Access to technologies and their benefits may be unevenly distributed.

questions.question_text: Why should society evaluate new technologies?

options.label: A
options.text: They may create both benefits and unintended risks

options.label: C
options.text: Every invention should automatically be rejected

questions.explanation: Technology may have economic, social, environmental, ethical, and security consequences.

questions.question_text: Which statement best represents responsible innovation?

options.label: A
options.text: Developing technology while considering safety, ethics, society, and environmental effects

options.label: B
options.text: Deploying every technology immediately regardless of risk

questions.explanation: Responsible innovation considers consequences as well as technical performance.

questions.question_text: Scientific development in Nigeria is supported by:

options.label: A
options.text: Universities, research institutes, government agencies, and industry

questions.explanation: Scientific work in Nigeria involves universities, specialised institutes, public agencies, industry, and other organisations.

questions.question_text: Agricultural research can contribute to Nigeria by:

options.label: A
options.text: Improving crop production and food security

questions.explanation: Agricultural research can improve productivity, resilience, disease control, and food security.

questions.question_text: Medical research in Nigeria is important for:

options.label: A
options.text: Understanding and responding to diseases affecting the population

questions.explanation: Health research supports understanding, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases relevant to the population.

questions.question_text: Scientific research commonly requires funding for:

options.label: A
options.text: Equipment, personnel, facilities, and data collection

questions.explanation: Research requires human expertise, equipment, infrastructure, materials, data collection, and analysis.

questions.question_text: Collaboration between universities and industry can help:

options.label: A
options.text: Translate research into practical products, processes, and services

questions.explanation: University-industry collaboration can help transform research outcomes into practical innovation.

questions.question_text: A major challenge to science and technology development in Nigeria can include:

options.label: C
options.text: A complete lack of scientific talent

questions.explanation: Funding, infrastructure, equipment, research capacity, and coordination can constrain scientific development.

topics.name: Ethics, Environment and Responsibility in Science

questions.question_text: Research ethics primarily concerns:
questions.explanation: Research ethics establishes principles for responsible, fair, and safe research conduct.

questions.question_text: Informed consent is especially important when research involves:
questions.explanation: Participants should understand relevant aspects of research and voluntarily agree to participate.

questions.question_text: Fabricating scientific data means:

options.label: A
options.text: Inventing results that were not actually obtained

questions.explanation: Fabrication is the unethical creation of false data or results.

questions.question_text: Environmental science helps society understand:

options.label: A
options.text: Interactions between human activity and natural systems

questions.explanation: Environmental science investigates interactions among humans, organisms, ecosystems, resources, and physical environments.

questions.question_text: Why is sustainability relevant to science and technology?

options.label: A
options.text: Development should consider long-term environmental and social consequences

options.label: C
options.text: Scientific activity has no environmental effects

questions.explanation: Sustainable development considers present needs alongside long-term environmental and social wellbeing.

questions.question_text: A scientist finds credible evidence that a widely used product may pose a serious public risk. The most responsible response is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Verify and report the evidence through appropriate scientific and regulatory channels

options.label: D
options.text: Publish an unsupported accusation without verification

questions.explanation: Responsible scientific conduct requires careful verification and appropriate communication of credible risks.
